title: Every route and endpoint is covered by at least one use-case
statement: For any repo whose inventory_coverage sensor reading is non-empty (routes[] or endpoints[] is non-empty), every route id in coverage-matrix.routes[] and every endpoint id in coverage-matrix.endpoints[] MUST appear in at least one links[] triad. Equivalently, coverage-matrix.unmapped.routes and coverage-matrix.unmapped.endpoints MUST both be empty arrays. Adopters with no frontend (endpoints-only) or no backend (routes-only) still apply: any route or endpoint that exists must be claimed by a use-case.
rationale: Brownfield adoption begins with surface inventories. An unmapped route or endpoint means a user-facing flow exists with no traceable specification — the inverse of the Architect's job, and the single highest signal that documentation is lagging code. Per Phase 17.D and D-57, this invariant gates the brownfield substrate: 17.C ships the sensors that produce the coverage matrix; 17.D requires the matrix to be fully bound. The 'gate' severity (Phase 10.A) blocks promotion without blocking development — adopters can land changes that introduce new routes/endpoints, but they cannot promote a release without first closing the use-case gap.

strategy.rationale: The registered test corpus provides deterministic regression evidence for this invariant.
